scope: Port thermal_pause (phone thermal-pause-*/pause-cpuN cooling devices) on the real sched_walt halt path

details: 4 cdevs (alias, default thermal-pause-<mask>, pause-cpuN without cooling-cells) max_state 1
pausing cpu3 drains 6 hogs; resume returns it
group (big cluster) pause, overlapping single pause keeps ownership
DT cooling map pauses/resumes via step_wise
unload while paused resumes the CPU

bugs_found_and_fixed: Port built without CONFIG_SCHED_WALT: linux/sched/walt.h turned walt_pause_cpus() into a stub returning 0, so pauses reported success without halting (first passing run was luck); ftrace showed zero halt_cpus events
Factory: resuming a group released CPUs still paused by another cdev (WALT keeps one vote bit per client); resume only unshared CPUs
WALT halt: RQCF_UPDATED was set only under CONFIG_SCHED_DEBUG (removed in 7.3, checks always on) -> clock assertions in move_queued_task; set unconditionally and update clock after relock
Factory lifetime: global list re-init per probe, resume work queued then freed, unregister under callback lock, unreferenced child nodes
walt_reverified: sched-walt 2/2 standard (6 checks), 4/4 sustained all-walt, zero warnings; CRC 340/39/11 imports match
